citations.quote: Current renderer supports labels but not a user-selected fill color. Preserve its existing label output.

existing_behavior: src/board.js line 1 renders a label as SVG text with no fill handling; tests/board.test.js line 4 locks render('A') to '<text>A</text>'; docs/limitation.md line 1 states labels work, fill color does not, and existing label output must be preserved.

options.description: Change signature to render(label, fill) where fill is optional; when omitted output is exactly the current string, when supplied output adds a fill attribute to the same text element.
options.label: Option A - Optional second fill argument with default preserving output
options.shows_it_works: Existing test render('A') === '<text>A</text>' still passes unchanged; new call render('A', 'red') returns text element with fill and same label.
options.tradeoff: Smallest delta and backward compatible, but positional argument does not scale if more style options are added later.

options.description: Change signature to render(label, opts) where opts is an optional object such as { fill }; when opts/fill is absent output is exactly the current string.

grounded_in.quote: Current renderer supports labels but not a user-selected fill color. Preserve its existing label output.

options.label: Option B - Optional options object with fill field
options.shows_it_works: Existing test still passes unchanged; render('A', { fill: 'red' }) returns same label with fill applied and render('A', {}) equals current output.
options.tradeoff: Extensible to future style fields without new positionals, but slightly more verbose for the single fill-color case.

options.description: Leave render(label) exactly as-is and add a new exported function that reuses render internally and adds fill handling.
options.label: Option C - Separate fill-aware function reusing render
options.shows_it_works: Existing test passes untouched with zero change to render; new function output contains the same label markup plus the requested fill.
options.tradeoff: Zero risk to existing behavior, but creates two parallel entry points and duplication the other options avoid.

question: How should the user-selected fill color be accepted while preserving the existing label output?
scope_proposed: Delta only: add user-selected fill color to the existing SVG board renderer without changing existing label output or existing tests. No rewrite of src/board.js logic, no edits to tests or fixtures.
task_text: Extend this existing SVG board renderer with a user-selected fill color. Its current label output and tests must keep working.
